speaker: Mr Leon Perera
text: asked	the Minister for Social and Family Development (a) how many Maintenance Record Officers (MROs) have been appointed to date; (b) how many cases of potentially recalcitrant defaulters have they investigated to date; and (c) whether the outcome of MRO investigations has succeeded in identifying cases where maintenance payments have been extracted from defaulters who were able but unwilling to pay and, if so, what is the number of such cases to date.

speaker: The Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Social and Family Development (Assoc Prof Dr Muhammad Faishal Ibrahim) (for the Minister for Social and Family Development)
text: Where appropriate, the Court can then impose harsher penalties against such defaulters.

speaker: The Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Social and Family Development (Assoc Prof Dr Muhammad Faishal Ibrahim) (for the Minister for Social and Family Development)
text: The MRO is not part of the Court process and is only deployed in cases directed by the judge.

speaker: Mr Leon Perera (Non-Constituency Member)
text: I believe that is what you said, but just to confirm that that is the case.

speaker: Mr Leon Perera (Non-Constituency Member)
text: Thirdly, in cases where spouses are unable to locate their ex-spouse who is supposed to pay maintenance to them, what avenues or recourse do spouses who are owed maintenance, have in such cases, if the person is just not contactable?

speaker: Assoc Prof Dr Muhammad Faishal Ibrahim
text: The answer to the first question is yes; it is only after the judge directs it and then the MRO will be activated.

speaker: Assoc Prof Dr Muhammad Faishal Ibrahim
text: With regard to the second and third questions, I think we need to look at a case, whether any divorce or even relationship issues, as a case where we want to see how we can facilitate relationships to still be connected for the sake of the children.

speaker: Assoc Prof Dr Muhammad Faishal Ibrahim
text: It is important for us not to jump to conclusions too early.

speaker: Assoc Prof Dr Muhammad Faishal Ibrahim
text: We want to give the opportunity for both parties to come to terms about how the maintenance can be agreed upon.

speaker: Assoc Prof Dr Muhammad Faishal Ibrahim
text: At the same time, it is also important for us to ensure that sufficient avenue is given and we want to see how we can facilitate this.

speaker: Assoc Prof Dr Muhammad Faishal Ibrahim
text: So, even after the MRO has been appointed, we realise that ex-couples or the parties involved are able to reach a common understanding, a common platform to see how maintenance can be paid or can be effected.
